title: collectReward is permissionless: any wallet can re-anchor rewardPerSecond at trivial cost, indefinitely extending the depletion tail
description: collectReward(amount) has no access control. Any wallet can deposit 1 wei every block; each call updates rewardPerSecond = (rewardBalance * PRECISION) / depletionDuration, re-anchoring the depletion clock against a near-unchanged balance. The combination of the V1 rate-recompute behavior and the permissionless surface means the effective depletion-per-second observed by stakers can be held near zero indefinitely.
impact: Stakers receive far less than the advertised depletion rate as a griefer keeps the rate-recompute near zero. Reward tokens are not stolen but their effective distribution is impaired — value sits parked in rewardBalance or accrues to far-future entrants instead of the staker cohort the funder intended to reward. Total griefer cost is 1 wei per call plus gas, trivially affordable on L2.
attackPath: Yield-accumulator funds collectReward(real_amount); rewardPerSecond set high.
Griefer calls collectReward(1) every block; each call re-anchors rewardPerSecond against the same (slightly increasing) rewardBalance over the full depletionDuration.
Effective rewards-per-second is suppressed near zero; stakers receive a tiny fraction of advertised yield.
Total griefer cost: 1 wei * N blocks plus gas — trivial on L2.
likelihood: medium — requires a sustained griefer; rational only if the griefer derives value from suppressing yield (short on protocol, holds competing position, social attack)
assumptions: No access control on collectReward (verified by reading code); attacker has trivial budget; V1 rate-recompute behavior (acknowledged known issue) amplifies the effect
externalRequirements: Griefer wallet with rewardToken balance >= 1 wei per call
recommendation: Either (a) restrict collectReward to a whitelisted funder (the stable-yield-accumulator) via onlyFunder modifier, or (b) enforce a minimum amount threshold (e.g., amount >= MIN_FUNDING_AMOUNT) that makes griefing economically unfeasible. Option (a) is preferred — the function semantically belongs to one role.
